attachments.text:
Sorry, I did not supply a minimal vimrc earlier, I only had a hunch of the problem. Anyways, I think now I've got a pretty clear picture of what is going on, after testing a bunch of stuff throughout the day.

The minimal vimrc would be:

```
call plug#begin('~/.vim/bundle')
Plug 'dense-analysis/ale'
Plug 'vim-denops/denops.vim'
Plug 'Shougo/ddc.vim'
Plug 'statiolake/ddc-ale'
call plug#end()
call ddc#custom#patch_global('sources', ['ale'])
call ddc#enable()

```

However, it's a bit unclear about what the correct fix would be. A summary of the issue is - Ale does not always respond with results, and in cases of rapid typing input, ddc pushes many consecutive requests to ale, but ale only remembers and fires the callback on the most recent one.

The code path starts here:  
<https://github.com/statiolake/ddc-ale/blob/master/denops/ddc/sources/ale.ts#L35-L41|https://github.com/statiolake/ddc-ale/blob/master/denops/ddc/sources/ale.ts#L35-L41>  
which calls into here:  
<https://github.com/statiolake/ddc-ale/blob/master/autoload/ddc/ale.vim#L8-L17|https://github.com/statiolake/ddc-ale/blob/master/autoload/ddc/ale.vim#L8-L17>  
Which in Ale, reaches into here:  
<https://github.com/dense-analysis/ale/blob/d098124e59ba38b0fcd97b41eec4a6de81bc09ab/autoload/ale/completion.vim#L833|https://github.com/dense-analysis/ale/blob/d098124e59ba38b0fcd97b41eec4a6de81bc09ab/autoload/ale/completion.vim#L833>  
At which point, it overrides a few buffer local variables that hold onto the callback and the request info, BUT only for the last call into GetCompletions (i.e. each subsequent call to GetCompletions overwrites all callback and info data for the previous call):  
<https://github.com/dense-analysis/ale/blob/d098124e59ba38b0fcd97b41eec4a6de81bc09ab/autoload/ale/completion.vim#L843-L845|https://github.com/dense-analysis/ale/blob/d098124e59ba38b0fcd97b41eec4a6de81bc09ab/autoload/ale/completion.vim#L843-L845>  
<https://github.com/dense-analysis/ale/blob/d098124e59ba38b0fcd97b41eec4a6de81bc09ab/autoload/ale/completion.vim#L867-L875|https://github.com/dense-analysis/ale/blob/d098124e59ba38b0fcd97b41eec4a6de81bc09ab/autoload/ale/completion.vim#L867-L875>

So basically we end up with requests into Ale's completion system, but we ultimately only respond with the latest callback, which leaves a bunch listeners that ultimately time out.

It would probably be a much bigger change to `fix` Ale to hold onto all requests and have all callbacks fire, but it would also create a lot of additional work for DDC to process requests that might be out of date. I did hack a bit on the ddc-ale plugin to vastly minimize request spam, but it's not ideal since if the number of results are huge, the max number might kick in and hurt your chances of finding what you are looking for:  
<https://gist.github.com/amadeus/9a438bc725d5892d7eedb754008c9928|https://gist.github.com/amadeus/9a438bc725d5892d7eedb754008c9928>

From an overall ddc architecture discussion though, it does kinda feel like ddc should be built in a way that the requests from these services may never come back, and at least give plugin devs a way to handle or catch a timeout, instead of just logging to echom.

*Problems summary*

After a while in a session, I start seeing msgpack timeout errors, and was wondering if there was an expectation here. I am pretty sure it's due to various sources never resolving their completion results. Is this something source authors need to ensure they handle properly? Or is this an error that ddc should suppress?

*Expected*

Not to see TimeoutErrors in the message logs

*Environment Information*

• ddc version (SHA1): `e392213`
• OS:  
    macOS
• neovim/Vim `:version` output:  
    macVim, 8.2, 1-3376

*Provide a minimal init.vim/vimrc with less than 50 lines (Required!)*

I am continuing to dig in and see if I can find a specific source of the problem, but figured I would start the dialogue about whether it's a plugin or ddc issue.

*Screenshot (if possible)*

<https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/83376/131395374-9c3b28e2-6b6b-423d-87f1-999775ded878.png|CleanShot 2021-08-30 at 12 39 08>
